Actual Article Body:
(Photo by Win McNamee/Getty Images)

Though the White House denied a recent report that the administration of President Donald Trump is slow walking anti-abortion action until after the 2026 midterm elections, pro-life advocates are warning that such considerations are unacceptable.

White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles led discussions with Attorney General Todd Blanche urging him to defer the Department of Justice’s actions involving abortion until after the midterm elections, The Washington Sun reported Friday. The White House, however, reportedly told the outlet such conversations “never occurred.” (RELATED: Why Does Susan Collins Oppose Confirming Blanche? One Reason Involves Abortion Pills)

The allegation, despite the denial, triggered backlash from pro-life leaders on social media.
